subject: Finovex — cost alignment & rollout plan (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finovex.com>, procurement@finovex.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Finovex — cost alignment & rollout plan (post-call recap)

Alex / Finovex team — thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side and clear next steps so we stay aligned.

Pain points & goals (as discussed)
- High per-call token spend driven by verbose authorization checks and rich context in each request (avg ~1.8k tokens / request).
- Bursty auth/transaction profile: peak 10–15x baseline during morning batch jobs and merchant settlement windows.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for auth flows; p95 < 100ms preferred for merchant-facing lookups.
- Primary constraint: initial monthly budget target ~$25k (pilot-stage cap) with an expectation to scale if ROI proves out.

Quick quant anchors we talked through
- Current estimate: ~1.2M tokens/day -> ~36M tokens/month at present load pattern (you mentioned spikes, will refine after sample).
- Pilot goal: demonstrate 25–40% effective token reduction via batching + KV prefix caching (depends on cache hit rate).
- If we achieve ~35% token reduction, rough TCO improvement on hosted plan is ~20–30% once we factor throughput/latency overheads.

Recommended pilot approach (6 weeks)
- Phase 1 (week 1): exchange workload samples and sample logs (I attached finovex-workload-sample.csv), enable limited logging access for our eval.
- Phase 2 (weeks 2–4): hosted pilot with tuned batching (target avg batch size 6–8 for auth flows), KV prefix caching enabled for session state, and focused telemetry collection.
- Phase 3 (weeks 5–6): produce TCO model & rollout playbook; recommend Dedicated pool sizing if sustained throughput and budget allow.

Proposed commercial framing
- Pilot subscription credits + professional time: we can structure as hosted credits (applied to token spend) plus 40 hours of engineering support for integration & tuning.
- If Finovex commits to Dedicated within 90 days of pilot, we can discuss a pilot-to-dedicated transition discount. Marissa will outline numbers below.

Immediate next steps (action items)
- Alex: share a 2-week log extract (anonymized) and confirm procurement contact for SOC2/VPC requirements.
- Procurement: confirm acceptable paperwork turnaround and whether DocuSign is preferred for the MPA.
- Marissa / Redwood commercial: share pilot pricing & draft MPA (Marissa, please attach).
- Karthik / Redwood infra: prepare a short perf/roi sensitivity model (batch sizes 2/4/8 and cache hit rates 10/30/50%).

Attachments: finovex-workload-sample.csv (small sample), redwood-draft-mpa.pdf (draft, redlines welcome).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the calendar invites for the technical deep dive and the procurement intro.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
redwood.com
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finovex.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finovex.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovex — cost alignment & rollout plan (post-call recap)

Thanks for the clear summary, Soojin — much appreciated. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: the $25k/mo is the finance-provisioned pilot cap. We could increase spend if you can show the 30%+ TCO improvement in the pilot window.
- Compliance: procurement will require SOC2 Type II evidence and a VPC/private connectivity option for production (they want to see network diagrams and KMS controls).
- Logs: happy to share a 2-week anonymized log dump. I’ll send a secure link to the Drive folder by EOD.

Quoted from your note: "If we achieve ~35% token reduction, rough TCO improvement on hosted plan is ~20–30% once we factor throughput/latency overheads." That’s the baseline finance will want to see modeled. Please include conservative and optimistic scenarios.

Procurement contact is procurement@finovex.com — they’ll expect DocuSign and a pointer to SOC2 artifacts.

We’re comfortable with the 6-week pilot timeline. Please keep the technical deep dive focused on how caching & batching impact latency for our auth path; our product team will join.

—
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Engineering | Finovex
alex.torres@finovex.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finovex.com>, procurement@finovex.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovex — cost alignment & rollout plan (commercial framing + next steps)

Looping in the commercial framing here so procurement and Alex have visibility. Soojin — great recap. Internal notes for our ask: 

Proposed pilot commercial offer (outlined)
- Hosted pilot credits: $15,000 in hosted credits applied to token/compute spend for the 6-week pilot period.
- Professional services: inclusive up to 40 hours (integration, telemetry, tuning). Additional hours billed at $250/hr.
- Pilot discount: we can offer a one-time 30% credit if Finovex converts to a 12-month Dedicated commitment within 90 days of pilot completion.

Key commercial asks from Finovex
- Procurement to confirm SOC2 acceptance criteria and expected MPA SLA targets (availability p95/p99).
- A PO or signed MPA to unlock the hosted credits (we can accept a shortened MSA signature for pilot).

Links / refs
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/289347 (ticket: FIN-3847)

Next internal steps
- Karthik: please prepare the three-case sensitivity model (conservative / mid / aggressive) using the batch/cache permutations Soojin listed; add latency delta for each case. Deliver by Tuesday EOD.
- Soojin: book the technical deep dive with Alex’s product team for Wed/Thu next week.

I’ll prepare the draft MPA (PDF attached in Soojin’s initial mail) and an executive one-pager for procurement.

—
Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finovex.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovex — cost alignment & rollout plan (technical notes)

Quick technical notes for the model and the deep dive: 
- Batching: auth path tolerates a windowed batch of 50–200ms; empirical batch sizes of 6–8 should be achievable without missing p95 targets for non-user-facing flows. For merchant-facing lookups we’ll model batch sizes 2–4 to prioritize latency.
- KV prefix caching: early estimate is 25–40% hit rate on session/context keys for your traffic shape; that translates to ~20–35% token savings depending on how much context is repeated.
- Quantization: I don’t recommend post-training 4-bit quant for the merchant quality bar; can evaluate 8-bit for background tasks but will include quality delta in the model.
- Metrics I’ll produce: token reduction %, net TCO delta, latency p95/p99 delta for each scenario, and a recommended Dedicated pool size if conversion looks attractive.

I’ll drop the spreadsheet link into the shared Drive and update Marissa’s HubSpot deal with the three-case numbers by Tuesday.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
